title: Chat stream pulse & resilient handler patterns
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: Customers integrating long-lived streaming chat connections report hard-to-debug stalls and partial outputs when network blips, proxy timeouts, or model-side GC pauses occur. Existing patterns either re-stream from scratch (duplicate tokens) or require large user-side plumbing to dedupe and resume. Goal: deliver a lightweight, battery-included pattern for SDK consumers that combines a small 'pulse' heartbeat for liveness detection, chunk-level checkpointing, idempotent event handler primitives, and retry/resume helpers that make it straightforward to build resilient chat UIs and batch consumers without forcing users to implement complex state machines.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes a StreamConductor helper with: start(), resume(checkpoint), stop() and an on_event(handler) registration API.
StreamConductor emits a periodic pulse event when no tokens arrive for configurable interval (default 3s) so UIs can show 'thinking' vs stalled.
SDK supports checkpointing at fragment boundaries (token groups with metadata) and a resume() helper that requests model continuation without duplicating already-committed tokens.
Retry policy baked into helper: exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 restores by default, and clear semantic signals to application code (recoverable vs terminal).
End-to-end integration test covering network drop+resume producing a single coherent transcript (no duplicates, correct token order) in <10s on CI using recorded responses.
Telemetry: spans that correlate initial request, each reconnect attempt, and final completion; metrics emitted for pulse_count, resume_attempts, and duplicate_token_rate (should be 0 in tests).
Documentation: a cookable example in the SDK docs showing a minimal UI and a server-side consumer implementing idempotent handler with provided utilities.
API review completed and no blocking backward-compatibility concerns with existing streaming APIs.
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamConductor (thin coordinator) that wraps existing streaming client socket and maintains fragment checkpoints (fragment_id, byte_offset, last_token_hash).
Pulse generation is internal timer-based; pulse event is lightweight and only emitted if no token events within pulse_interval. Pulse should be opt-out via config pulse_interval=None.
Checkpointing rules: only checkpoint at 'commit' fragment boundaries (user-visible message boundaries). Avoid checkpointing every token to limit state size.

Resume protocol: client includes last_checkpoint metadata in resume request; server-side model variants or runtime should support continue_from_checkpoint semantics (fallbacks for runtimes that don't by replaying a short prompt).

Backpressure: conductor exposes a consumer buffer with configurable max_pending_bytes. When buffer is full, conductor emits backpressure warnings and can switch to low-throughput mode (smaller request window).
Telemetry: add trace id propagation header, instrument resume attempts as child spans, increment metrics counters via observability client in runtime.
API ergonomics: favor callback and async iterator interchangeably. Example utilities: .events() async generator and .on_event(fn) registration for callback-based apps.
Make default retry policy conservative; add hooks for applications to supply custom RetryPolicy implementations via simple callables.
Avoid changing low-level stream protocol; implement conductor entirely in SDK to remain compatible with hosted and dedicated deployments.
Security: do not persist checkpoints containing user PII. Checkpoints should be opaque token hashes and offsets only.
progress_updates: 2026-02-10 - Ticket created. Collected customer bug reports and examples from Support. Identified major pain points: duplicate tokens on reconnect and long recovery UX.
2026-02-15 - Spike complete: prototype conductor that uses token-hash checkpointing and a pulse timer. Verified we can resume against local mock runtime by injecting continue_from_checkpoint flag.
2026-02-19 - First API sketch reviewed with SDK leads; switched from 'resume_from_token_id' to 'checkpoint object' to avoid leaking token internals. Added pulse opt-out.
2026-02-23 - Implemented async generator facade .events() and simple .on_event(). Wrote unit tests for pulse emission timing and basic resume handshake mocking network drop.
2026-02-27 - Integration test flake observed on CI when resume reconnects after 7s; root cause: race in buffer flush. Added explicit drain step before sending resume metadata.
2026-03-01 - Telemetry spans wired up to tracing client. Preparing PR for internal review (draft).
testing_plan: Unit tests: pulse timer thresholds, checkpoint encoding/decoding, retry policy backoff math.
Integration tests: simulated socket drop at various points (mid-fragment, between fragments); ensure resume produces single coherent transcript.
Load test: 100 concurrent stream conductors with bursty token rates to validate memory boundedness of buffer and verify backpressure signals.
Manual test: small electron UI sample to validate pulse UX and duplicate suppression in live q/a scenario.
Telemetry validation: assert the presence of spans and metrics after simulated failures in test harness; duplicate_token_rate must be zero.
Security review: static scan for checkpoint leakage of user content; smoke test with PII-shaped payloads to ensure no plaintext persisted in checkpoints.
Canary rollout: enable feature flag for 5% of org customers in staging then 20% in prod, monitor resume_attempts and errors.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some backends cannot fast-forward a model from an opaque checkpoint. Mitigation: conductor will fall back to a short 'replay' prompt constructed from last N tokens (configurable) to reconstruct state.
Risk: Pulse event could generate noisy UX for very low-latency streams. Mitigation: default pulse_interval is 3s; consumers can tune or disable it.
Risk: Checkpoint format could change and invalidate stored state across releases. Mitigation: version checkpoint payloads and provide migration helpers; keep checkpoints opaque.
Risk: Excessive memory use for long-lived streams. Mitigation: bounded buffer with eviction strategy and explicit guidance in docs for large transcripts (periodic external persistence obligations).
Risk: Duplicate suppression logic may miss edge cases. Mitigation: include deterministic token hashing and multiple integration tests; instrument metrics to detect non-zero duplicate_token_rate.
